To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The multisurface model predicts the activities of Cu, Cd, Ni, and Zn well.
the model predictions are in good agreement with the measured metal activity data for Cu, Cd and Ni, but not for Pb.

the activity of metals in soils can be predicted by the model reasonably well over a broad concentration range, but that the contribution of the individual sorption surfaces to metal binding varies with the metal and its loading.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the role of the different soil components on heavy metal sorption and speciation in soils.
the prediction of metal binding by soils and the development of models for metal speciation and bioavailability.
the development of an approach to predict the activity of metals in soil and the contribution of various soil sorbents to this activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soil organic matter plays a major role in binding of metals, but that the role of clay silicates and iron hydroxide cannot be neglected.
soil organic matter and clay minerals are the main sorbents that control the activity of heavy metals in sandy soils.

the activity of Cu, Zn, Cd, and Ni in sandy soils with different sorbents is controlled by the organic matter and clay silicates, while for Pb it is controlled by both organic matter and iron hydroxide surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activity of heavy metal ions is mainly determined by soil organic matter, and that the contribution of clay minerals and iron hydroxide surfaces to metal binding becomes increasingly important with increasing metal loadings.

soil organic matter plays a key role in controlling the activities of Cu2+ Cd2+, Zn(2), and Ni2+ but that clay silicates are also important in the binding of these metals when soil organic matter content is low.
the multisurface model is a useful tool for predicting the behavior of metals in sandy soils with different organic matter and clay contents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil organic matter, especially humic acid, is the most important soil sorbent in sandy soils for Cu2+, Cd, Zn, Ni, and Pb.
the contribution of different sorbents to metal binding varies considerably with the metal of interest and with the soil properties.
a multisurface model can be a valuable tool in the evaluation of metal binding in soils.
